_note: Feature centers (deg, planetocentric, east-positive) and diameters (km) are from the USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, read 2026-10-31. 'summit' snaps to the highest DEM point within radius_km of the center; 'rim' snaps to the highest point on the ring between ring_km[0] and ring_km[1] that is a local peak (no higher ground within 1 km radially or 1.5 deg along the ring). 'fixed' uses the coordinates as given.

sites.name: Lunar South Pole
sites.about: The geographic pole itself. It sits on the sloping edge of Shackleton crater, so nearby ground blocks part of its sky: a good example of why the exact spot matters.

sites.name: Shackleton rim high point
sites.about: Highest point on the rim of Shackleton, a crater whose floor never sees the Sun.

sites.name: de Gerlache rim high point
sites.about: Rim of de Gerlache crater, near the ridge linking it to Shackleton.

sites.name: Shoemaker rim high point
sites.about: Rim of Shoemaker, a large permanently shadowed crater.

sites.name: Mons Malapert summit
sites.about: A massif facing Earth, long proposed for its view of Earth.

sites.name: Faustini rim high point
sites.about: Rim of Faustini, a permanently shadowed crater. (Nobile's rim was left out: its highest crest is the summit of Mons Mouton.)

sites.name: Mons Mouton summit
sites.about: A broad plateau mountain between Nobile and Malapert, targeted by commercial landers.

sites.name: Mons Cabeus summit
sites.about: Mountain near Cabeus, the crater LCROSS impacted to find water.

sites.name: Apollo 11 (contrast)
sites.about: Equatorial site for contrast: no terrain data here, so a smooth-sphere horizon is used.
